questions.question_text: What is the lowest common multiple of 8 and 4?

options.why: 32 is a common multiple but is not the lowest one.
4 is not divisible by 8.
16 is a common multiple but 8 is the smaller positive common multiple.

questions.solution_text: 8 is divisible by both 8 and 4, and no smaller positive number is divisible by 8, so the LCM is 8.

questions.question_text:
Two numbers are written as the product of their prime factors as shown: $2\times3^2\times7$ and $2\times3\times5$.
Which of these is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of the two numbers?

options.why: Uses only the common prime factors and omits factors needed for a multiple of each number.
Uses only one factor of 3 instead of the highest power $3^2$.
Does not include the distinct prime factors 5 and 7.

questions.solution_text: The LCM uses each prime at its highest power: $2\times3^2\times5\times7=630$.

questions.question_text: “The lowest common multiple of two different prime numbers is their product” Is this statement...

options.why: Distinct prime numbers have no common prime factor to alter their product.
The product of distinct primes is always a common multiple.

options.text: (D) Impossible to say without more information
options.why: The prime-number conditions provide sufficient information.

questions.solution_text: Different prime numbers have no common factors apart from 1, so their least common multiple is found by multiplying them together.
